text:
Koreans don't ask "how old are you?" They ask "what year were you born?"

Because in Korea the birth year, not the birthday, decides who's older. Born in 2000? You're a 00년생, and everyone born in 1999 is your senior. Even if their birthday is in December and yours is in January.

What year are you? 👇

text:
How Koreans would write your name:

Olivia → 올리비아
James → 제임스
Sophie → 소피
Michael → 마이클
Chloe → 클로이
Daniel → 대니얼

Koreans spell by sound, not letters. So Michael is 마이클, never 미카엘.

text:
Oppa, unnie, hyung or noona?

It depends on two things: whether they're older, and YOUR gender.

A woman calls an older man oppa, an older woman unnie.
A man calls an older man hyung, an older woman noona.

And born in January or February before 2003? There's a whole exception called 빠른년생.

text:
Korean has two number systems and you need both at the till.

One item: 하나 (hana) → 한 개
Two items: 둘 (dul) → 두 개
But ₩2,000 is 이천 원 (icheon won), from the other system.

Say 두 개 주세요 (du gae juseyo, two please) and you'll sound like you've been here a while.

Late November: a proper coat. Mornings get close to freezing.

Climate Card: unlimited rides inside Seoul for a fixed price.
